definition: Describing something that is either very firm and close, or not firm and allows movement.
example: The new screws were tight, but the old ones were loose.

definition: A long, hollow tube through which water, gas, or oil can flow.
example: There was a leak in the old water pipe in the basement.

definition: Related to your feelings and thoughts, rather than to your external appearance or surroundings.
example: To achieve your goals, you need to find your inner motivation.

definition: To make it difficult for someone to do something or for something to happen.
example: Lack of funding can tend to hinder progress in research.

definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently.
example: The engineers are checking if the new bridge design is technically feasible.

definition: Without success; useless.
example: We tried to repair the old car for hours, but it was all in vain.

definition: A situation in which there is not enough food for a great number of people, causing illness and death.
example: Conflict and drought led to a widespread famine in the region.

definition: To live in a place.
example: The remote island is inhabited by many rare species of birds.

definition: Problems or difficulties.
example: I always have trouble with understanding complex math problems.

definition: To be suspended or attached from above, often freely.
example: Bats often hang upside down in caves while they sleep.

definition: A person's way of thinking and their opinions.
example: Understanding the mentality of teenagers is important for educators.

definition: Many; involving more than one.
example: The exam included a difficult multiple choice section.

definition: A part or share of a whole.
example: A large proportion of the students passed the test.

definition: To shake slightly, especially because of nervousness, fear, or cold.
example: The child began to tremble with fear after hearing the loud thunder.

definition: To tell someone something confidently to remove doubt.
example: The doctor tried to assure the patient that the surgery would be successful.

definition: Describing something that is either not able to be cured or able to be cured.
example: Some diseases are incurable, while others are easily curable with medicine.

definition: Clearly separate and different from others.
example: Despite their similarities, the two cultures remain distinct.

definition: Used to show that you think a word or phrase is not accurate or true.
example: His so-called 'friends' left him alone when he needed help.

definition: The ability to do something successfully or efficiently.
example: She showed great competence in her new role.

definition: Describing something that is either against the law or allowed by the law.
example: It is illegal to drive without a license, but it is legal to walk on the sidewalk.

definition: Demanding that rules be obeyed exactly.
example: The teacher was very strict about deadlines.

definition: Feeling worried or anxious.
example: I felt uneasy about leaving my dog alone all day.

definition: A place where you stay, especially temporarily.
example: Many students live in a lodging house while attending university.

definition: To own or have something.
example: Always keep an eye on your personal possessions when traveling.

definition: A general agreement among a group of people.
example: After a long discussion, the committee was able to reach a consensus.

definition: To support yourself against something or someone.
example: When times are tough, it's good to have a friend to lean on.

definition: Describing something that is either not likely to happen or likely to happen.
example: It's improbable that it will snow in summer, but it's probable that it will rain tomorrow.

definition: To form or be a part of something.
example: Women constitute a large percentage of the workforce.

definition: A set of related things that follow each other in a particular order.
example: The instructions must be followed in a specific sequence.

definition: To protect someone or something from harm or attack.
example: Soldiers bravely defend their country against enemies.

definition: To consider something as being caused by someone or something else.
example: She attributes her success to hard work and dedication.

definition: A formal suggestion or plan, or an offer of marriage.
example: He surprised her with a romantic marriage proposal on their anniversary.

definition: To demand something forcefully, not accepting any refusal.
example: She insisted on paying for the whole meal herself.

definition: A friend, or someone you work or study with.
example: My work mate helped me finish the project on time.

definition: To find yourself in a place or situation that you did not intend or expect to be in.
example: If you keep driving without a map, you might end up getting lost.

definition: Very large, heavy, or solid.
example: The company made a massive profit last year.

definition: A measurement in one direction, such as length, width, or height.
example: Architects often work with models in three dimensions.

definition: Not direct or immediate.
example: The grammar lesson covered how to report statements using indirect speech.

definition: Almost real; created by computer technology and appearing to exist but not physically real.
example: Virtual reality games are becoming very popular.

definition: Exceptional intellectual or creative power or natural ability.
example: Albert Einstein was a scientific genius.

definition: The state of being with other people; a guest or guests.
example: I enjoy reading a book when I don't have company.

definition: A residential area or district situated on the outskirts of a city.
example: Many families prefer to live in a suburb outside the busy city center.

definition: The land along the edge of a sea, lake, or wide river.
example: We walked along the sea shore collecting shells.

definition: To send someone away; to officially remove someone from their job.
example: The manager had to dismiss the employee for repeated lateness.

definition: To wound or pierce with a sharp-pointed part, often injecting poison.
example: I accidentally stepped on a bee and got a bee sting on my foot.

definition: A particular quality in your personality.
example: Honesty is a valuable personality trait.

definition: To formally announce that you are leaving a job or position.
example: He decided to resign from his position after many years of service.

definition: The reporting of a particular important event or subject.
example: Many news channels provided live coverage of the election results.

definition: To change continually; to vary in an irregular way.
example: The price of oil can sharply fluctuate due to global events.

definition: A lack or shortage of something.
example: Many people suffer from iron deficiency, which can cause tiredness.

definition: A period of relaxing, sleeping, or doing nothing after effort or strain.
example: After a long day of work, I need some rest.

definition: To behave in the way that is expected or required.
example: Students are expected to conform to the school's rules.

definition: Not likely to change or fail; firmly established.
example: After the accident, the patient was reported to be in a stable condition.

definition: To make someone want to do something, especially something that involves hard work and effort.
example: Good teachers know how to motivate their students to learn.

definition: A desire to harm, annoy, or offend someone.
example: In spite of the heavy rain, we still went for a walk.

definition: To consider or think of someone or something in a particular way.
example: Many people regard her as a talented artist.

definition: A person who is an expert in a particular area of work or study.
example: He went to see a heart specialist for his condition.

definition: Used to introduce more exact and detailed information.
example: There are two main problems, namely, lack of funding and lack of staff.

definition: A part of an animal or machine that allows it to fly.
example: The bird spread its wings and flew away.

definition: A group of sports teams that play against each other, or a group of people, countries, etc. that have similar interests or goals.
example: Our football team is currently at the top of the league.

definition: Happening or done in a natural, often sudden way, without any planning or thought.
example: Her spontaneous reaction to the good news was a loud cheer.

definition: Of little value or importance.
example: Don't worry about such a trivial problem; it's not worth your stress.

definition: To eat dinner, especially in a restaurant.
example: We often dine out at our favorite Italian restaurant on weekends.

definition: Lasting for the whole of a person's life.
example: Many universities promote the idea of lifelong learning.

definition: To take something important or necessary away from someone.
example: War can deprive children of education and a normal childhood.

definition: A strong desire or impulse.
example: I had a strong urge to open the present before my birthday.

definition: To control or manage; to give instructions to someone or something.
example: He dreams of becoming famous and directing a film one day.

definition: In a different way or in all other respects; or else.
example: You must study hard; otherwise, you might fail the exam.

definition: A part of an area of activity, especially of a country's economy.
example: Many nurses and doctors work in the public sector.

definition: The basic nature or most important quality of something.
example: The painting captured the true essence of the city.

definition: To consider or think something to be true.
example: I reckon him to be one of the best players on the team.

definition: The greatest possible amount or level.
example: The maximum speed allowed on this road is 100 km/h.

definition: Evidence or argument establishing a fact or the truth of a statement.
example: There is no clear proof that he committed the crime.

definition: Impressive and large in size, scope, or extent.
example: They held a grand party to celebrate their anniversary.

definition: To change something slightly, especially to make it more effective or suitable.
example: It took some time to adjust to the new working environment.

definition: To hit your open hands together, usually repeatedly, in order to show approval or to attract attention.
example: The audience stood up to give the performers a big clap.

definition: To pass an illness from one person or organism to another.
example: Mosquitoes can transmit diseases like malaria.

definition: Something valuable won in a competition or lottery.
example: She was very excited to receive a prize for her excellent essay.

definition: The space between two lines or surfaces that meet.
example: The photographer shot the building from an unusual angle.

definition: The ability to see.
example: Regular eye exams are important for maintaining good vision.

definition: The intervening time.
example: The report will be ready next week; in the meantime, please review these notes.

definition: To arrange for people to come together for a formal meeting.
example: The committee will convene next Tuesday to discuss the new policy.

definition: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.
example: Having empathy for others is a crucial part of being a good leader.

definition: To let something fall; to make something become lower in amount or level.
example: The company had to drop the prices sharply to attract more customers.
